topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence
target_audience: Advanced Undergraduate Physics or Engineering Students

sections.title: The Turbulence Puzzle: Defining the Chaos
lecture_lines: Turbulence is chaotic, unpredictable fluid motion.
The Reynolds Number governs this complexity.
It compares inertial to viscous forces.
High Re creates chaotic, swirling eddies.
Finley the trout navigates these flows.
animations: Create text 'Turbulence is complex fluid motion.' with #FFFFFF color.
Draw a large eddy separating into smaller eddies.
Highlight energy moving from large to small scales.
Final scene showing full cascade in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Kolmogorov’s Hypothesis: The Energy Cascade
lecture_lines: Energy cascades from large to small scales.
Large eddies break down into smaller ones.
This process continues until viscous dissipation.
animations: Show large energy injection pulse at scale L.
Display small eddies absorbing energy with #FFFF00 arrows.
Fade to black, illustrating energy decay through scales.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Constant (C_K)
lecture_lines: C_K is a universal turbulence constant.
We see this in a -5/3 slope.
animations: Write equation E(k) = C_k * epsilon^(2/3) * k^(-5/3) in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the -5/3 slope graph on log scale.

sections.title: Dissipation Scales: Where Constants Meet Reality
lecture_lines: Viscosity dominates at the Kolmogorov scale.
Kinetic energy converts into internal heat.
The dissipation range is fluid specific.
animations: Illustrate viscous forces damping motion at Kolmogorov scale.
Show transition from inertial range to dissipative range.
Zoom into micro-scale, visualizing heat release in #FF0000.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: Statistical laws simplify complex flow modeling.
We predict turbulence without tracking particles.
Order exists within chaotic statistical systems.
animations: Summarize cascade concept with summary text.
Reiterate the role of C_k in turbulence models.
